builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Efficient Benchmarking in Production: A Study of an Evolving LLM Agent
summary: The method replaces full benchmark reruns for recurring production-agent evaluation with a small fixed subset of questions stratified by difficulty, selected once from historical runs. It costs a one-time calibration over past evaluation data and accepts a small score-estimation error (around 1 percentage point MAE for the best variant) in exchange for roughly 60% fewer executions per evaluation cycle. It can fail if the agent's behavior drifts so that the fixed subset's difficulty profile no longer discriminates, or if historical calibration data are unavailable for a new agent family, although the paper reports transfer across five families and stability with one-day calibration windows.
rationale: Fixed stratified subsets require no infrastructure beyond existing evaluation runs, directly cut recurring API or GPU evaluation costs by more than half, and the authors validate stability and cross-agent transfer on real production data.

claims.statement: The method replaces full benchmark reruns for recurring production-agent evaluation with a small fixed subset of questions stratified by difficulty, selected once from historical runs. It costs a one-time calibration over past evaluation data and accepts a small score-estimation error (around 1 percentage point MAE for the best variant) in exchange for roughly 60% fewer executions per evaluation cycle. It can fail if the agent's behavior drifts so that the fixed subset's difficulty profile no longer discriminates, or if historical calibration data are unavailable for a new agent family, although the paper reports transfer across five families and stability with one-day calibration windows.

Executing 200 questions (38.5% of a full run) with multidimensional 2PL adaptive testing yields 1.03 percentage points of MAE in score fidelity; deployed difficulty-stratified fixed subsets achieve comparable recurring-evaluation cost reduction and transfer to five other agent families without recalibration.
